channel.title: Research Notes — Mohsen Mofidi Chelan
channel.description: Research notes on Chinese foreign policy, China–Middle East relations, strategic narratives, leadership perceptions, and foreign-policy decision-making.

item.title: Beyond Rhetorical Adoption: Chinese Narratives and Elite Causal Beliefs in Iran and Saudi Arabia
item.description: Chinese ideational influence should be measured through changes in elite causal beliefs, not rhetorical agreement or policies favourable to Beijing.

item.title: Can Stories Get You Killed? Narrative Unfalsifiability and Strategic Entrapment
item.description: Considers whether political narratives become strategically dangerous by preventing actors from recognizing failure; proposes 'narrative unfalsifiability' as a link to weak strategic learning and conflict persistence.

item.title: From Development Partner to Order-Shaping Actor: China’s Strategic Narrative in the Middle East
item.description: China’s Middle East narrative increasingly links development and sovereignty to selective diplomacy and a multipolar regional order.
